content.title: About
content.content: The Cheeseburger Slider is a mini version of the classic cheeseburger, served as small patties in a bun. It contains a beef patty, melted cheese, pickles, onion, ketchup and mustard. A typical serving consists of 3‑4 pieces, perfect for a quick snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sliders first appeared in the United States in the early 2000s as a convenient way to sample several burger variations in one order.
The small size allows restaurants to offer mixed trays with different flavors, such as bacon, spicy sauce, or pineapple.
In some eateries sliders are presented on wooden boards to emphasize a “home‑style” feel.
The combination of cheese and beef in a compact portion makes them more calorie‑dense per 100 g than a regular cheeseburger.
Cheeseburger sliders are often used in “eat‑in‑a‑minute” challenges because of their bite‑size format.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The beef patty provides a complete set of essential amino acids needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese adds calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat is rich in vitamin B12 and niacin, which aid nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Beef supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The blend of protein and fat provides quick energy, useful for active lifestyles.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Because of the meat, cheese, and sauces, sliders can be calorie‑dense; moderation is important for weight management.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Melted cheese and beef contain saturated fats, which may raise cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Condiments and pickles add significant sodium, a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy should choose dairy‑free alternatives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheeseburger sliders are served hot, often in paper wrappers. They are easy to eat with your hands, paired with dipping sauces, fries, or a fresh side salad. Adding avocado or crispy onions can enhance the flavor profile.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked sliders in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C for up to 2 days. For longer keeping, freeze them in an airtight container for up to 1 month; reheat in an oven or microwave before serving.
